filename: Estimating the Kinetic Energy Spectrum from the Second-Order Velocity Structure Function using a Regularized Fitting Approach.pdf
title: Estimating the Kinetic Energy Spectrum from the Second-Order Velocity Structure Function using a Regularized Fitting Approach
testbed_rationale: The study develops an optimization-based physical diagnostic framework to reconstruct kinetic energy spectra from velocity structure functions rather than producing a machine learning parameterization benchmark dataset.
pain_points: Analytical inverse Hankel transform is ill-conditioned due to the oscillatory Bessel kernel, finite separation range, and sampling noise.
Uncertainty in structure function SF2 at large spatial separations propagates into reconstructed KE spectra at low wavenumbers.
Noise in SF2 obscures the precise detection and localization of spectral slope transitions across dynamical regimes.
Overparameterization leads to Jacobian rank-deficit and numerical instability when the number of spectral segments approaches or exceeds the number of data points.
Instrumental sampling issues (e.g., drogue loss in drifters) reduce effective sample size and degrees of freedom at large spatial separations.
extraction_notes: The paper uses classical regularized non-linear least squares optimization (Trust Region Reflective algorithm via scipy.optimize.least_squares) rather than deep learning or statistical machine learning models. The year 2026 appears on the preprint header and in references (e.g., Gutierrez-Villanueva et al. 2026).
